why: creates the guard condition ON THE EXECUTOR and returns `(HandleId, GuardCondition)`. rclrs constructs a `GuardCondition` from a `Context` and adds it to a wait set; rclrs's wait-set machinery; the reason is stated in full at `cpp:WaitSet`. so the executor has to own the flag -- it lives in the arena, which is what makes the handle `Send + Sync` with no allocation. SINCE phase-417 W4.e this is the ours-only PRIMITIVE, not the verb a Rust user reaches for: `NodeCtx::create_guard_condition` is the node-level spelling (see `rust:NodeCtx::create_guard_condition`) and it calls `register_guard_condition_on(Some(node_id), ..)`, so a node-created guard inherits that node's `SchedContext` like every other handle the node makes. The executor form stays because an image with no node -- a bare `Executor::open` plus a wake source -- still has to be able to make one. See `c:guard_condition_set_callback` for the three-owner state this ended.
